title: Torres Del Paine and tonal-based color adjustment (Part 3, 2022) — Photoshop landscape workflow

date.basis: embedded_creation_time indicates export date; transcript provides no corroborating shooting date

summary: This instructional video presents a practical Photoshop workflow for turning a landscape sequence into a cohesive image through sky-focused selection, multi-plane focus considerations, and advanced tonal/color grading. The presenter guides sky assessment and crop decisions, discusses focus stacking ambiguities and manual blending when frames have misaligned planes, builds directional light and zone-based tonal structure, and progressively strongens color and atmosphere with blur, luminosity, and selective color adjustments. The sequence culminates in perspective widening, cloud augmentation, and a tonal-based color adjustment to unify colors across disparate regions. The transcript emphasizes non-destructive layering, iterative passes, and careful masking-by-painting rather than heavy masking, with attention to keeping eye flow toward the light source and preserving depth cues in mountains and water.

sections.title: Sky assessment and initial crop
sections.description: Identify the best sky in the sequence and choose a starting crop, with a preference for wider 4x5 framing to emphasize the sky and its color as a compositional driver.

sections.title: Focus stack planning and frame selection
sections.description: The speaker recalls a potential focus-stack approach and contemplates whether the sequence supports stacking; notes that different frames may be sharp at different planes, affecting future blending decisions.

sections.title: Manual focus blending and edge-aware merging
sections.description: When automated stacking is impractical, a manual blend is performed by aligning a focal point and cloning from that edge to merge foreground and background, using a harder brush to preserve edge integrity along water.

sections.title: Lighting direction planning and initial zone thinking
sections.description: The presenter emphasizes developing directional light from the side and shading features toward that light; introduces the concept of viewing the scene in zones (sky/reflective zones, mountains, foreground) to structure subsequent edits.

sections.title: Two-zone and three-zone color planning and initial grading
sections.description: The shot is framed as multiple zones (sky+reflection, mountains, and fall-colors) with early color and tonal adjustments to unify these regions while retaining the directional light cue.

sections.title: Blur + luminosity haze layering and atmosphere separation
sections.description: A blur plus luminosity workflow is introduced to create atmospheric haze; a clone-paint approach is prepared to reuse the adjustment across multiple areas and layers for consistent diffusion.

sections.title: Layer separation of mountains and edge refinement
sections.description: Manual separation of mountain layers is performed to establish depth; edges are carefully erased and refined to ensure clear separation between layers (e.g., towers named Fortaleza and others) and to maintain believable depth cues.

sections.title: Enhancing horn lighting and aggressive color sculpting
concepts: masking to affect only illuminated areas
sections.description: The horn peaks are given intensified lighting through targeted adjustments; the workflow uses 50-150 and selective color to selectively illuminate only the illuminated portions, while preserving surrounding context.

sections.title: Perspective widening and cloud augmentation
sections.description: A wide-angle illusion is pursued via perspective warp (rule of trapezoids) and selective distortion plus scale; a larger cloud is duplicated and inserted to push the eye toward the light source.

sections.title: Tonality stabilization via tonal-based color adjustment
sections.description: The core tonal-based color-adjustment technique is demonstrated: reduce overall saturation, cool shadows, restore neutral blues/greys in distant shadows, reapply highlights incrementally, and refine colors across zones to achieve a cohesive, natural look.
